title: the harbor map answers at cairn codemother harbor_master
intention: 'cairn codemother harbor_master show map open' prints the harbor map, as outline 9.4.1.5 names it, and operator_inbox's one-status proof and probe read the map there.
why: Measured 2026-11-13: test_one_status_everywhere.py has 3 teeth red, 'cairn harbor_master show map open exited 127' (the device left class-space in 6ae83e7e1); 'cairn codemother harbor_master' answers "no such verb 'harbor_master'".
traces_to: RULE 1 (the proofs reach the map only by command) and Law 9 (the outline is the spec; the code changes).
how: A word script cairn/devices/codemother/0/bin/harbor_master passes only status queries (show/get/list, 9.4.1.5) and asks harbor_master on the bus through the bus_client's published mouth. The harbor's map/get views take --filter as a dict arg through the base handler (35b92c5de7ef), so its list-args overrides go. The proofs and probes call `cairn codemother harbor_master show map --filter open`. Where the machine berths is a follow-up (outline 9.4.1).

clauses.claim: 'cairn codemother harbor_master show map --filter open' exits 0 and prints the map's rows; a non-status verb exits 2 naming 9.4.1.5
the three one-status teeth are green reading the map through that command, and still red if a report wears a second label

decisions.text: D1: a codemother word script, 0/bin/harbor_master, routes status queries (show, get, list) to harbor_master on the bus via python3 -m cairn.tools.bus_client; any other verb exits 2 (9.4.1.5). The self-named launcher is not reached by bin/cairn for a word, so the word is its own file.
D2: test_one_status_everywhere.py:263, probes/one_status_everywhere.py:73 and system_word probes/his_case_never_bites.py:147 call ('codemother','harbor_master','show','map','--filter','open').

D3: harbor_master device.py's map/get views take filter as a keyword (the base view-args dict); its own list-args _handle_get/_handle_show overrides are deleted; test_the_map_wears_the_one_label.py sends args {'filter': 'open'}.
